CENTRAL Station.
October 24 1922

REPORT ON Arrival of the S.S. "Shin Yu"

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by J. K. Owens A.I.

Sir,

The S.S. "Shin Yu" arrived in Shanghai from
Vladivostock via Chefoo at 3 a.m. October 24 and the passengers
were landed at the Custom Jetty at 9.50 a.m. The ship's
complement of foreign passengers were 11 male, 11 female and
7 children. Ten passengers were disembarked at Chefoo for
Harbin. Nineteen Chinese passengers also arrived in Shanghai
by the "Shin Yu".

The vessel left Vladivostock on October 16 at
which time the town was comparatively quiet but events were
expected to develop quickly. Many of the civil population are
moving to Harbin and two ships of the Russian Volunteer
Fleet left Vladivostock for Chefoo with full complements of
passengers during the last few days. It is said that General
Dietrichs is gathering all his officers together and sending
them to Port Inkou, north of Port Arthur, so that an influx
of officers into Shanghai is unlikely. Two more vessels
are leaving Vladivostock for Shanghai immediately viz : the
S.S. "Laurestan" of Messrs L. V. Lang & Co. and a Chinese
vessel the name of which I was unable to ascertain. Many
people are said to be desirous of leaving Vladivostock but
either have not got the money or owing to the shortage of
vessels cannot get passages. There is now apparently no
supervision over passports or other credentials of persons
leaving Vladivostock.

the S.S. "Shin Yu" were Mr. Merzaloff, late Chief of the

1922年10月24日

关于“新裕”轮（S.S. "Shin Yu"）抵达的报告

由警探长 D. I. Sullivan 呈报，经助理督察长 J. K. Owens 转呈

先生：

“新裕”轮于10月24日凌晨3时从符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）经烟台抵达上海，乘客于上午9时50分在海关码头登岸。该船外籍乘客共计男性11人、女性11人及儿童7人。十名乘客在烟台下船前往哈尔滨。另有十九名中国乘客乘“新裕”轮抵达上海。

该船于10月16日离开符拉迪沃斯托克，当时该市相对平静，但预计局势将迅速变化。许多平民正迁往哈尔滨，在过去几天内，俄国志愿船队的两艘船只满载乘客从符拉迪沃斯托克驶往烟台。据称，迪特里希斯将军（General Dietrichs）正在集结其所有军官并派往旅顺港以北的营口港，因此不太可能有大量军官涌入上海。另有两艘船只即将从符拉迪沃斯托克驶往上海，即：L. V. Lang & Co. 公司的“劳雷斯坦”轮（S.S. "Laurestan"）以及一艘中文名未能查明的中国船只。据说许多人渴望离开符拉迪沃斯托克，但要么因缺乏资金，要么因船只短缺而无法获得舱位。目前看来，对于离开符拉迪沃斯托克的人员，其护照或其他证件已无监管。

在乘“新裕”轮抵达上海的乘客中，有梅尔扎洛夫先生（Mr. Merzaloff），前任

Vladivostock Criminal Police. He states that he was obliged
to leave as disorders are expected and owing to his energetic
measures against criminals he would be one of the first against
whom revenge would be sought in the event of a "Red" occupation
of the town. Colonel Boulakoff, late passport examining
officer on the frontier at Pogranichnaya, also arrived on
the s.s. "Shin Yu". He gave the same reasons for leaving as
Mr. Merzaloff. Colonel Boulakoff is going to live at 70
Broadway Terrace, and Mr. Merzaloff whose wife and family
have been in Shanghai since July 22, 1922, at 73 Range Road.
Mr. Merzaloff does not speak English.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Sullivan.

Translation of extracts from Russian Newspapers.

"Our Speech"
(Nasha Rech")
Vladivostok,
12 -10- 1922.

Japanese information on the Korean Revolutionaries.

Tsuruga, 1-29-1922. At the beginning of July the Korean
Provisional Government in Shanghai entered into a contact
with the Communists in Harbin.
An agreement has been come to with the Chita Government
that after the evacuation of the Japanese troops the Korean
Provisional Government would remove from Shanghai to
Nikolsk-Ussurisky.
Chita's consent was obtained in the middle of August
simultaneously with the declaration of the Japanese
Government regarding the evacuation of troops.
Then three representatives of the Korean Government
were sent to Nikolsk to make preparations for the removal
of the Government; after they had arrived at Nikolsk they
established their agencies at Shkotovo and Spassk and
keeping in contact with the Chita Government, began acting
as organizations for unifying the Koreans residing in the
Maritime Province.
Furthermore they had to start Red propaganda in Korea,
but as the crossing of the Korean Frontier has been made
difficult, they began, in conjunction with the Harbin
Communists, spreading their proclamations at Dzinsan, Fusan,
Gensan, Tonsin and other places.
A strong propaganda of Bolshevist ideas and the
re-establishment of Korea's independence are also their
general intentions.

"Our Speech"
14- 10- 1922.

An information from the Possiet-Bay district states that
the evacuation of this district will be completed on October
20. In this connection the Korean Revolutionaries residing
at the Possiet district are forming Partisan-detachments
for the purpose of establishing Korean National Authority
over this district. Although their attempt to organize
Partisan-detachments do not excite general interest among
the local Koreans who wish to conserve peaceful relations
with Russians, the latter are alarmed at the actions of
Korean Revolutionaries and many Russians are leaving for
Vladivostok.

俄文报纸摘录译文。

《我们的言论》
("Nasha Rech")
符拉迪沃斯托克，
1922年10月12日。

日本方面关于朝鲜革命者的情报。

敦贺，1922年1月29日。7月初，位于上海的朝鲜临时政府与哈尔滨的共产主义者建立了联系。
已与赤塔政府达成协议，在日本军队撤军后，朝鲜临时政府将从上海迁至乌苏里斯克（Nikolsk-Ussurisky）。
赤塔方面的同意是在8月中旬获得的，与此同时日本政府发表了关于撤军的声明。
随后，朝鲜政府派遣三名代表前往乌苏里斯克，为政府迁移做准备；他们抵达乌苏里斯克后，在什科托沃（Shkotovo）和斯帕斯克（Spassk）设立了机构，并与赤塔政府保持联系，开始作为统一居住在滨海边疆区的朝鲜人的组织进行活动。
此外，他们本应在朝鲜境内开展红色宣传，但由于穿越朝鲜边境变得困难，他们便与哈尔滨共产主义者合作，开始在津山（Dzinsan）、釜山（Fusan）、元山（Gensan）、唐津（Tonsin）等地散发他们的宣言。
大力宣传布尔什维克思想以及恢复朝鲜独立，也是他们的总体意图。

《我们的言论》
1922年10月14日。

来自波西耶特湾（Possiet-Bay）地区的情报指出，该地区的撤离工作将于10月20日完成。为此，居住在波西耶特地区的朝鲜革命者正在组建游击队分队，旨在在该地区建立朝鲜民族政权。尽管他们组织游击队分队的尝试并未引起希望与俄罗斯人保持和平关系的当地朝鲜人的普遍兴趣，但后者对朝鲜革命者的行动感到恐慌，许多俄罗斯人正前往符拉迪沃斯托克。
